days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Abisko
stops.detail: It runs primarily as a trekking route from Abisko (northern end) to Hemavan (southern end) through the almost uninhabited Scandes.

stops.name: Sälka
stops.detail: From Abisko to Sälka, the Kungsleden is part of the cross-border Nordkalottleden.

days.title: Kebnekaise Massif and National Parks
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Kebnekaise
stops.detail: The hiking route between Abisko at the national park of the same name in Norrbotten County and Hemavan at the Vindelfjällen wilderness reserve in Västerbotten County includes a "detour" via Kebnekaise – Sweden's highest mountain and a planned national park – to Nikkaluokta.

stops.name: Nikkaluokta
stops.detail: Due to its remoteness, the Kungsleden can only be accessed from (listed from north to south) Abisko, Nikkaluokta, Saltoluokta (or Kebnats to the south and Vakkotavarre to the north on Länsväg BD 827) Kvikkjokk, Jäkkvik, Adolfström, and Hemavan.

stops.name: Stora Sjöfallet
stops.detail: In addition, a section of the trail runs through the UNESCO World Heritage site Laponia – the Stora Sjöfallet National Park and on the edge of the Sarek National Park – as well as the Pieljekaise National Park.

stops.name: Kvikkjokk
stops.detail: Only the northern half between Abisko and Kvikkjokk is more heavily traveled, and especially between Abisko and Kebnekaise or Nikkaluokta, particularly due to the annual trekking event Fjällräven Classic by the equipment manufacturer of the same name.

stops.name: Vindelfjällen
stops.detail: In the Kebnekaise region and in Vindelfjällen lives a part of Sweden's rare Arctic fox population (Swedish "Fjällräv").

stops.name: Hemavan
stops.detail: The airports of Hemavan, Gällivare, and Kiruna near the northern Kungsleden are also served by direct flights from Stockholm.
